title: Elastic Beanstalk: deploy code, AWS runs the stack

kcs.statement: AWS Elastic Beanstalk is a PaaS-style service: you upload application code and it provisions and manages the EC2 instances, load balancer, Auto Scaling group and health monitoring for you.
With Elastic Beanstalk you keep full access to the underlying resources it creates, and the service itself is free; you pay only for those resources.
Elastic Beanstalk supports common web platforms such as Java, .NET, Node.js, Python, PHP, Ruby, Go and Docker, so standard web apps deploy without designing infrastructure.

problem_ideas: A team of two developers has a Node.js web app and no ops staff: which deployment service, and what does it create for them?
A Beanstalk app's bill shows EC2 and ELB charges but no 'Beanstalk' line: explain why.
After deploying with Beanstalk, an engineer wants to change the instance type: can they? Where?
Which of these does Beanstalk not handle for you: capacity provisioning, load balancing, writing application code, health monitoring?
Sort three requirements (template every resource, upload a .war file, run a function on an S3 upload) to CloudFormation, Beanstalk or Lambda.
A Docker-packaged web app must go live today with auto scaling: is Beanstalk a valid option?
